title: Recap Video Ideas: How to Make a Party or Event Recap Reel
description: Recap video ideas for parties, weddings and trips: a shot list, a hook-build-peak structure, beat math, music rules and 9:16 export settings for posting.
dek: Ten formats, a shot list and the export settings for a 15 to 45 second reel.
excerpt: Ten recap formats, the shots to grab during the event, how to cut to the beat, which music is safe to post and the 9:16 export settings for Reels, TikTok and Shorts.
secondary_keywords: how to make a recap video

faq.q: How long should a recap video be?
faq.a: For a party, wedding or trip, 15 to 45 seconds is the sweet spot, and 30 seconds is a good default. That’s long enough for a hook, a build, a peak and an end card, and short enough that people watch it twice. YouTube Shorts accept up to 3 minutes, but a recap rarely needs that long.

faq.q: What is the best app to make a recap video?
faq.a: CapCut is the most flexible free option, with templates, auto captions and Auto Cut beat syncing. Edits, Instagram’s free editor, suits people who post mainly on Instagram. iMovie is better for widescreen edits. If you want the recap built for you from every guest’s photos, Filmsera makes one automatically when the film develops.

faq.q: What should be in an event recap video?
faq.a: Cover six kinds of shots: an establishing shot, details like the cake or the table, arrivals, faces mid-laugh, motion such as dancing, and the peak moment, then finish on a quiet ending. Twenty to forty short clips of 2 to 5 seconds give you enough to cut a 30-second recap with options.

faq.q: Can I use any song in a recap video?
faq.a: On a personal account, the safest route is to add the song from Instagram’s or TikTok’s own library when you post. Baking a commercial song into the file can get the post muted, blocked or removed. Businesses should use pre-cleared libraries, such as TikTok’s Commercial Music Library, or royalty-free tracks they hold the rights to.

faq.q: What size should a recap video be for Instagram and TikTok?
faq.a: Export at 9:16 vertical, 1080×1920 pixels, at a fixed 30 frames per second, as an MP4 or MOV with H.264 video. Keep text away from the edges, especially the bottom third, where captions and buttons sit, so nothing important gets covered when the reel plays.

faq.q: How do you make a recap video from photos only?
faq.a: Treat it as a photo-dump reel. Pick 15 to 30 photos, order them hook, build, peak and end, and cut on the beat: half a second per photo on a fast song, 1 to 2 seconds on a slower one. A gentle zoom on each photo adds motion, and one text card at the end gives context.
